messages:
marisol-hr: Quick thread 1: contractors converting to FTE - how do we handle level and comp during promo cycles?

tony-manager: We have two contractors converting in June. One might be L4-ish. Do we need a full promo packet or is convert + level change simpler?

nina-eng: From previous runs, conversions are separate form 'Hire Convert' + optional promo packet if level differs from initial band. @marisol-hr can confirm.

marisol-hr: Correct. Process: 1) Submit Convert Request form (Recruiting -> HR) with proposed title/level. 2) If level > the standard conversion baseline, submit a Promotion Request alongside it. The comp committee treats them like a normal promotion.

ryan-recruiting: FYI the baseline we offer for contractor->FTE is usually the midpoint of the band unless manager requests above. If requesting above midpoint, include market comps in the note.

tony-manager: Is there any difference for equity grants on conversion vs internal promo?

marisol-hr: Equity: conversions get a standard RSU grant based on level and tenure equivalency. Promotions can trigger refresh grants, but that's discretionary and goes through comp+rewards. Flag it in the packet if equity is a retention concern.

compbot: [automated] Note: All compensation exceptions require VP approval and may delay processing by one payroll cycle.

nina-eng: Another question: what happens if the convert is effective before comp committee meets? Can we set a placeholder salary and then retro-adjust?

marisol-hr: You can set an offer that is conservative; if comp approval increases salary, payroll will run a retro adjustment for any days between effective date and approval, as long as approval is within 30 days. If outside 30 days, we need exec sign-off for retro beyond window.

tony-manager: For the promotion part, what's the evidence we should include for an engineer who was a contractor? We don't have formal performance reviews.

marisol-hr: Include: 1) work samples (PRs, project docs), 2) manager summary of scope increase and impact, 3) 2 peer notes (can be from internal collaborators), 4) any client feedback if applicable. Keep it concise one-line headline + 3 bullets.

ryan-recruiting: Who signs the packet? Hiring manager + People Ops partner? And any recruiting OK?

marisol-hr: Manager + recruiting confirm background checks complete + People Ops comp partner sign-off for salary. Recruiting attaches candidate record and confirms start date.

nina-eng: Are there hard limits if the requested comp goes above band or market 90th? We're trying to be fair and keep equity.

compbot: [automated] Reminder: Upload market comp docs for any request > band top. Exceptions need VP+ approval.

marisol-hr: If above band top, you must include two external comp points (levels.fyi, surveys) and a business justification. These are rare but doable for critical hires.

tony-manager: Timeline question: we plan to convert 2026-06-15. Comp committee meets 2026-06-10. If packet misses that, will payroll apply change for 06/15?

marisol-hr: If packet is approved by committee on 06-10 and feeds are sent before payroll cutoff (06-12), yes. If it misses that committee, it goes to the next committee and effective pay will be later; you can request retro but subject to rules above.

ryan-recruiting: Is there a special code for headcount type change in the HRIS? I want to make sure internal dashboards update.

marisol-hr: Recruiting should set 'HC Type' = "Contractor -> FTE" in the hire form. People Ops will process the level and comp fields after approval; org chart and HC dashboards refresh nightly.

nina-eng: Helpful. One last: do managers need to announce conversions differently if comp isn't finalized? We don't want to promise numbers.

marisol-hr: Recommend announcing title and start date only. Hold off on sharing comp until official offer paperwork is ready. If there's a retention bonus, coordinate with People Ops to confirm wording.

tony-manager: Got it, thanks team. I'll start two packets and ping once forms are in.

compbot: [automated] Ticket CV-2026-49 opened for June comp reviews.
